headlines.title: G7 countries to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil reserves
headlines.description: Group of Seven countries agreed to release tens of millions of barrels of diesel fuel and crude to cap soaring gas prices.

headlines.title: Tracking U.S., state and county gas prices, in maps and charts
headlines.description: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

headlines.title: Hawaii’s picturesque Hōlei Sea Arch collapses into the ocean
headlines.description: The Google Maps red pin for the Hōlei Sea Arch, a rugged, 90-foot bow formed by 550-year-old lava flows and the prolonged sculpture of the salty Pacific, now states, “Permanently closed.”

headlines.title: U.S. labor market slows with midterms on the horizon
headlines.description: The U.S. labor market slowed during the month of September, according to new data Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

headlines.title: Tony Romo out as NFL analyst for CBS Sports following July DUI arrest
headlines.description: Tony Romo is out as an NFL analyst for CBS Sports following his July arrest on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, the network said Friday.

headlines.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. is getting a new name: Skydance
headlines.description: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison reveals Paramount and Warner Bros. will operate under the “Skydance” name following their merger. Entertainment journalist Brian Balthazar shares the latest on the acquisition and the company’s upcoming rebrand.

headlines.title: October Freebies: Doughnut, Hockey, Knife Skills Course, More
headlines.description: There are plenty of ways to get free things this October, and NBC’s Vicky Nguyen joins TODAY to share a round up. Her no-cost finds include a knife skills course, a Krispy Kreme doughnut and more!

headlines.title: Inside Look at How Retailers Use Your Data for ‘Price Experiments’
headlines.description: Across retail, travel, food and more, some companies are charging consumers different prices for the same products and services. Lindsay Owens, author of the new book “Gouged: The End of a Fair Price and What That Menas for Your Wallet,” says companies overcharge by using “price experiments” where they change randomly between customers and some also use “surveillance or personalized pricing” where they charge prices based on your data all to increase profits. headlines.title: Consumer Hot Topics: Spam Calls, Credit Safety and More
headlines.description: NBC’s Vicky Nguyen joins TODAY to answer viewer questions on everything from spam calls to travel insurance.

headlines.title: For the same ticket on StubHub, different prices for different people
headlines.description: NBC News volunteers saw eight different prices for the exact same Harry Styles ticket on StubHub. The company said it’s running random price experiments.

headlines.title: Should you bring iced coffee to a job interview? Question brews generational debate
headlines.description: What started as a conversation about job interview tips online escalated into a generational debate over whether it’s taboo to show up with an iced coffee to talk to a potential employer.

headlines.title: U.S. pressures European allies to release diesel reserves as Trump considers export ban
headlines.description: The Trump administration asked European allies to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
